entities.name: Penal Transportation (Exile Colonies)
entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: Britain transported 162,000 convicts to Australia (1788–1868), thousands more to the American colonies. France sent prisoners to Devil's Island (French Guiana). Convicts provided cheap labor for colonial expansion. Transportation solved two problems: overcrowded prisons and labor-starved colonies.
